## The question

[LinkedIn logo in Latex](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/190927/linkedin-logo-in-latex), asked by [texfan](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/28569/texfan) on TeX Stack Exchange (2014-07-10; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> How could I get a LinkedIn logo (like those found in http://press.linkedin.com/Media-Resources?SubjectID=644) in Latex?
>
> I found some tikz code somewhere, but that was not for one in blue, and it didn't look quite the same.
>
> Example:
>
> ![Enter image description here][q-1]
>
>   [q-1]: t0C80.jpg
:::

I think the simplest path is to use the EPS logos provided.  With `pdflatex` you will have to convert the EPS file to PDF, but there are many ways to do that (see https://tex.stackexchange.com/q/2872/1402) including “automatically” as in my installation.  If you download the [LinkedIn logo “bug” as EPS](https://brand.linkedin.com/downloads), you get a file `LinkedIn-InBug-2C.eps`.  Then use something like this document:

```latex
\documentclass{standalone}
\usepackage{graphicx}
% https://tex.stackexchange.com/q/190927/1402
\begin{document}
\raisebox{-0.35ex}{\includegraphics[width=2.5ex]{LinkedIn-InBug-2C}}%
linked.in/johndoe
\end{document}
```

and you get this:

![sample code output][1]

I had to manually adjust the `width` and `\raisebox` arguments to get the size and vertical placement right.  There might be other ways.  



  [1]: 8NSEp.png
